{"kind":"spec","title":"Phase 2 design changes: tool merges, start_work batching, dedicated agents","body":"## Intent
Execute the phase-2 design changes of the token-efficiency redesign on the stable post-Phase-1 surface: collapse the 21-tool surface to 14, merge the task-start round-trip into one gate-first call, and move invariant brief prose into dedicated user agents — each measured against the phase-0/1 baselines.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. The three tool families are merged: `specd_read` (view=show|query|dashboard), `specd_import` (mode=preview|apply|revert), `specd_store` (action=status|register|reference). Query filters (kind/status/q/of/insight/limit/store) and dashboard views remain reachable through the merged tools.
2. The total registered `specd_*` tool count is 14, verified by the harness static layer.
3. `specd_start_work` performs, in order: assertCanStartWork → create-or-reuse worktree → append work.started → returns {path, branch, status}. Re-running on a paused task reuses the existing worktree and does not duplicate events. A gate refusal happens BEFORE any side effect (no orphaned worktree).
4. `specd_open_pr` appends `work.completed {pr}` after recording `pr.created` (the review gate is already enforced inside it).
5. Command prompts (/spec run, /spec run waves) and the AGENTS.md/docs references use the renamed/merged tool names.
6. Dedicated user agents `specd-worker` and `specd-reviewer` exist in the dotpi agent config, carrying the naming convention, surgical-changes rules, docs/Diataxis rules (worker) and review dimensions (reviewer) ambiently. RUN_PROMPT worker/reviewer briefs shrink to task-variable data (title, body, scope, branch, spec intent).
7. A repo ↔ ~/.pi sync story for the agent definitions is documented in the repo (README or agent/ docs).
8. Every phase-2 slice ends with the harness re-baselined (SPECD_UPDATE_BASELINE=1) and the refusal matrix unchanged (7 pass / 16 refuse).

## Acceptance criteria
- `npx vitest run` green in packages/specd after each task; the harness static test passes with the re-seeded baseline (tool count 14).
- The e2e replay (SPECD_E2E=1) runs the flow through the review verdict: work.started recorded exactly once per task, review verdict lands, orchestrator turn count does not increase vs the phase-1 baseline (12 turns).
- The refusal matrix ok-flags are byte-identical to phase 1.
- The e2e replay runs successfully with the dedicated agents and its baseline diff shows the orchestrator prompt shrinking.

## Out of scope
Reviewer model/thinking right-sizing experiments (separate measured iteration); docs/*.md authoring cleanup; any gate or consistency-rule change (DO-NOT-CUT); GitHub issue/board surface changes.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"plan","title":"Phase 2 approach: merges → start_work → dedicated agents","body":"Technical approach for spec-0001 (phase 2 design changes):

1. Tool merges first (biggest surface change, everything else renames against it): one read tool (`specd_read(view=show|query|dashboard)` — shared store-resolution + per-view renderers), one import tool (`specd_import(mode=preview|apply|revert)` — mirrors the /spec import command dispatch), one store-bootstrap tool (`specd_store(action=status|register|reference)`). Registration, command prompts, and README updated in the same slice; harness re-baselined (count 14).

2. Execution-seam batching: new `specd_start_work(item)` = assertCanStartWork → create-or-reuse worktree → append work.started → {path, branch, status}; the worktree creation moves AFTER the gate so refusals leave no orphans; re-runs on paused tasks reuse the worktree and skip duplicate work.started events. `specd_open_pr` folds the `work.completed {pr}` append into its post-condition. RUN_PROMPT/RUN_WAVES_PROMPT collapse to the merged calls.

3. Dedicated user agents: `specd-worker` and `specd-reviewer` defined in the dotpi agent config (extending the existing specd-worker integration-test precedent), carrying naming/surgical/docs rules and review dimensions ambiently; RUN_PROMPT briefs shrink to task-variable data. Sync story: the agent/ directory in the repo is the source of truth; dotpi install/sync mirrors it into ~/.pi.

Decisions/baseline tracking: each task ends with `npx vitest run` + harness re-baseline (SPECD_UPDATE_BASELINE=1) + refusal-matrix check; the git diff of the baseline JSONs is the per-phase evidence (D8). Risks: merged-view param bloat (mitigate: per-view docs stay terse); idempotency edge on work.started (test both paths); agent-config coupling (mitigate: agents remain plain md/json definitions in agent/).","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}
{"decision":"merge order: tool merges first (everything renames against them), then execution-seam batching, then dedicated agents; per-task harness re-baseline as evidence"}

{"kind":"spec","title":"Rebase repo workflow from grill to specd","body":"## Intent
This repo's own development workflow and knowledge base are built on the grill extension: planning history lives in grill's `.pi/knowledge/atoms.db` (tracked in git), and AGENTS.md/README.md use grill as the canonical pattern example. Rebase the repo onto specd: specd is the canonical workflow and knowledge store (`.spec/`), grill knowledge is migrated once and retired, and docs lead with specd. The grill package itself stays as a fully working installable extension — it just stops being this repo's base.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. Migrate knowledge: run `specd_import_apply(source=<repo root>, apply=true)` to import all 31 grill atoms (16 decisions, 7 plans, 4 specs, 1 research, 3 validations) and their 16 links from `.pi/knowledge/atoms.db` into the `.spec` store (mostly application layer). A re-run must skip already-imported items (idempotent via imported origin_id).
2. Verify before delete: after import, `specd_dashboard` shows the imported items and a sample atom body (e.g. dec-0001) is readable in the store. `.pi/knowledge` is removed only after this verification passes.
3. Retire the grill knowledge base: `git rm -r .pi/knowledge` (atoms.db is the only tracked file under it). After the commit, `.pi/knowledge/` no longer exists in the tree or in git tracking.
4. AGENTS.md rebase: no grill-as-pattern references remain — the extension-pattern example cites `packages/specd` (store + gates + pipeline, event-sourced, code-enforced); grill appears only in the package list; the "Working on extensions" section stays accurate for all four packages.
5. README.md rebase: the extensions list and repository layout keep grill as one of four extensions, but the narrative leads with specd as this repo's development workflow; no framing presents the repo as grill-based.
6. Repo checks pass after all changes: `npm run check` and `npm test` are green; `git status -sb` clean after the commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- `specd_dashboard` shows all 31 imported items with their 16 links; re-running the import changes nothing (idempotency).
- `.pi/knowledge/` is gone from both the working tree and `git ls-files`.
- `grep -ri grill AGENTS.md README.md` shows grill only as an extension/package name — never as the repo's workflow or pattern basis.
- `npm run check` and `npm test` pass.
- Changes committed; working tree clean.

## Out of scope
- No changes to `packages/grill` source, tests, or package README — the extension stays fully functional.
- No changes to `agent/` config (grill is not referenced in `agent/settings.json` packages; install surface unchanged).
- No changes to `packages/specd` or new specd features.
- No `.gitignore` changes — the accidental `*.spec` ignore that covers `.spec/` stays as-is; the store is intentionally local-only.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

1. **Knowledge migration.** Run `specd_import_apply(source=<repo root>, apply=true)` against the repo root. Verify with `specd_dashboard` (expect 31 imported items, 16 links) and `specd_show` on a sample (e.g. the imported dec-0001 body). Idempotent — re-run is a no-op.
2. **Retire grill knowledge.** After verification: `git rm -r .pi/knowledge` (atoms.db is the only tracked file; the dir's .gitignore/.gitattributes are untracked and go with the rm -r... they're untracked so plain `rm -rf .pi/knowledge` after `git rm` of the tracked file).
3. **AGENTS.md.** Replace the grill pattern reference ("See packages/grill … for the model") with the specd store+gates+pipeline example; keep the four-package list and commands section accurate; example command can stay `packages/grill` only if still natural, else switch to another package.
4. **README.md.** Reword the extensions line and repository layout so specd leads as this repo's development workflow; grill stays listed as an extension with its one-line description.
5. **Check & commit.** `npm run check`, `npm test`, then a single commit (knowledge migration + docs) — `git status -sb` before committing per repo rules.

{"kind":"constitution","title":"dotpi: reproducible Pi config as code, with guardrails","body":"## Purpose
dotpi is my Pi configuration kept as code, mirroring `~/.pi` — a reproducible dotfiles-style setup with guardrails. It is not a generic package manager. Two halves: the Python installer/manager (`src/dotpi/`, launched via `./dotpi`) and the TypeScript Pi extensions it installs (`packages/`: specd, grill, jina, android-cli, wandb), plus vendored agent skills under `.agents/skills/`.

## Principles
1. **Never write `~/.pi` directly.** Every mutation goes through `./dotpi install|sync|backup|restore`.
2. **Guardrails are load-bearing.** Mutating installer commands require `-y` non-interactively by design; do not loosen them for convenience.
3. **Credentials never enter the repo.** Real keys live in the shell environment; `agent/auth.json` is placeholders/env references only. Never commit or print real credentials.
4. **Mirror discipline.** The repo is mirrored into `~/.pi` — run `git status -sb` before committing and only commit what you mean to install later.
5. **One extension pattern.** Every package: TS ESM, Biome (tabs + double quotes), `src/` sources + `test/` vitest suites, thin `src/index.ts` registration, pure logic in tested modules, explicit `.js` import suffixes.
6. **Checks before finishing.** `npm run check` (biome + tsc) and `npm test` for TS work; `python3 -m unittest discover -s src -t src` for the installer.
7. **Tests use fixture homes.** Installer tests never point at the real `~/.pi` unless explicitly asked.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

type=decision

## 1. Vision

`grill atom` (rename of grill kb) is a **repo-scoped atomic knowledge graph**: every unit of durable
knowledge is an **atom** (a typed node with a status, provenance, and an md body), and the value is
in the **bonds** (typed edges) between atoms.

The engine is deliberately small:

- **SQLite graph** (`.pi/knowledge/kb.db`) — nodes, edges, statuses, provenance.
- **md canon bodies** — prose lives in files: loose `nodes/*.md` bodies or promoted paths in `docs/`.
- **4 native tools** so AI sessions can walk the graph in-session; `/atom` commands for humans.

Research anchors (re-grounded 2026-10-08):

| Source | Finding applied |
| --- | --- |
| AKM / "Sustainable Architectural Decisions" (Zdun et al.), adr.github.io, MADR | Connecting + maintaining decisions are the named success factors; supersession links are first-class |
| Debt-aware ADR model (hartiga.de) | Decisions must carry explicit drawbacks/risk — statuses + supersession edges make debt visible |
| Zettelkasten atomicity guide (zettelkasten.de) | One building block per atom; links > folders; structure notes as entry points; over-engineering warning |
| Agent-memory survey 2026 (Awesome-Agent-Memory) | Dominant validated patterns: local-first SQLite+FTS, typed-edge graph memory, provenance-tagged bundles, md-wiki KBs, staleness workflows |

No vector DB, no MCP server, no new infra until a recipe measurably fails.","pathScope":"grill-atom","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"approved"}

## 3. Core decisions (from the grill session)

1. **Absorb the YAML graph into atom.** Extend the node-type enum (e.g. `requirement`, `concept`,
   `flow-stage`, `spike`), migrate all graph nodes + edges into kb.db, deprecate the YAML registry.
   Philosophy reconciled: SQLite holds graph/metadata; prose lives in md bodies (loose `nodes/*.md`
   or promoted `docs/` paths). The YAML file was the format exception.
2. **Edge graph is the spine.** Slice 2 imports supersession/dependency edges from the YAML graph at
   init; manual curation after. Everything else (pruning, staleness, digests, agent walking) hangs
   off edges.
3. **Map first, then physical cleanup.** Atom produces the live/retired/redundant map (dashboard);
   physical `docs/` restructure of the reference repo happens last, guided by that map.
4. **Rebrand to "grill atom".** Commands `/atom init|doctor|query|digest`; native tools
   `atom_query`, `atom_digest`, `atom_link`, `atom_backfill`; `/kb` kept as deprecated alias for one
   release. No MCP server — pi extension `registerTool` is enough.
5. **Canon naming: `NNN-slug.md`.** Promoted ADR paths become `docs/adr/026-unified-native-orchestration.md`
   (kebab slug, no `ADR-` prefix). Consequence: in-prose refs like "ADR-018" lose the filename grep
   path — doctor/query must resolve `ADR-NNN` ↔ `NNN-slug` aliases during migration.
6. **Workflows = recipes, not features.** Atom is the engine. Research, task/issue management,
   design/PRD (mermaid diagrams live in md bodies), learning paths are usage recipes over the
   existing 9 node types + digest task lenses. New engine features only when a recipe measurably fails.","pathScope":"grill-atom","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"approved"}

{"kind":"application","title":"Design: specd — spec-driven development extension for pi (clean-room, event-history store, adaptive pipeline, tier-model sinks)","body":"---

original_id=spec-0001
original_status=draft
scope=specd
---

# Design — Spec-Driven Development Extension (working name: `specd`)

**Scope:** everything in this document lives inside the extension's own package (`packages/specd`) and its `.spec` data. Nothing else in the host repo changes except what the root glob auto-wires (`pi.extensions: ["packages/*/index.ts"]`).

## 1. Purpose & positioning

A **new, clean-room** pi-coding-agent extension for spec-driven development (SDD). It is *not* a remake or redesign of `packages/grill` — it is built from scratch with a different goal — while consciously evolving grill's ideas: interview-driven elicitation, a local SQLite knowledge store, and event/revision history. The finish line of a planning cycle is a **dev-team task set on a development platform** (six supported platforms in v1 — see §4.5).

Differentiators vs researched rivals (spec-kit 1.0, openspec):
- **SQLite store instead of repo markdown** — repos stay clean; knowledge is queryable and event-sourced.
- **Evolution is first-class** — one append-only event history per work item; refinement is a designed stage, not a workaround (spec-kit's #775 pain is designed out structurally).
- **Small, stateful command surface** — one canonical command; no phase ladder to memorize.
- **Living-spec + full audit subsumes all three spec-kit persistence models** (flow-back / flow-forward / living spec) — spec as source of truth, revisions as events, audit trail free via time travel. Not a config; a property.

## 2. Goals / non-goals

**Goals (v1)**
1. One canonical, state-directed command drives the whole cycle: explore → spec → plan → tasks → export, with gates enforced from the event history — plus spec-kit-grade quality gates: requirements checklist, cross-artifact consistency check, and an append-only convergence loop.
2. Full execution loop in v1: task → worker subagent in an isolated git worktree → PR → status flows back into store and sink.
3. Vendor-neutral task/cycle schema with pluggable sink backends; **null sink** (project management entirely in the store) is the floor; **six adapters in v1**: GitHub, Linear, Jira, Notion, Trello, ClickUp.
4. Data migration from grill: atoms + edges import as provenance events (full design in `spec-0002`).
5. Per-sink onboarding: guided, plain-language setup for each non-GitHub platform.
6. UX bar: responsiveness/completeness at or above rpiv-ask-user-question; no half-rendered states.

**Non-goals (v1)**
- No grill code reuse (grill UI deemed buggy — unresponsive, incomplete, cut off).
- MCP transports for sinks (direct APIs in v1; MCP optional later).
- Process customization/presets and org catalogs/governance (post-v1).
- Per-event undo UI; whole-cycle branching/replay.
- No repo-wide concerns: the extension touches only its own package and `.spec` data.

## 3. Hard constraints

1. **Task-sink tier model (anti-lock-in):** null sink floor → **six first-class adapters in v1** (GitHub, Linear, Jira, Notion, Trello, ClickUp). Core schema speaks only vendor-neutral concepts (lanes, tags, states, assignment); sink-specific fields live in adapter metadata.
2. **Migration path from grill** must exist (designed in `spec-0002`).
3. **Low memorization UX:** one canonical command; optional verb commands only as convenience (two doors, one mental model).
4. **Clean-room:** no grill code; conceptual lineage + data migration only.
5. **Plain vocabulary:** user-facing terms are business-general and junior-safe; technical terms internal only.

## 4. Architecture

The pipeline is **agent-sequenced and code-gated**: specd registers a minimal tool set (`specd_create_item`, `specd_append_event`, `specd_add_link`, `specd_export`, `specd_dashboard`) plus a flow prompt; the interactive agent sequences the stages conversationally, while the store state decides legality and the tools refuse illegal transitions (e.g. export of an unapproved spec is refused in code, not by prompt compliance). Detailed M1 application in `spec-0003`.

### 4.1 Package layout (working name `packages/specd`)
- `index.ts` — thin: registers the canonical command, optional verb commands, and extension tools.
- `store/` — SQLite event-history store (`node:sqlite` stdlib `DatabaseSync`, zero native deps, grill's proven pattern; fresh schema: events, items, links, projections; FTS index).
- `pipeline/` — adaptive pipeline stages and gates (pure logic, unit-tested).
- `elicitation/` — questioning layer built on **rpiv-ask-user-question** (chosen machinery; replaces grill's custom picker/TUI).
- `research/` — **jina** extension integration: explore-stage web research with findings stored as evidence events on the item.
- `backends/` — task-sink adapters: `null` (store-native floor) + six platform adapters (§4.5).
- `execution/` — **pi-subagents** integration: worker subagents, worktree isolation, PR creation, reviewer subagents, status flow-back.
- `migrate/` — grill import (design in `spec-0002`).
- House conventions: pure modules + colocated tests, biome (tabs, double quotes), explicit `.js` import suffixes.

### 4.2 Store: one shared event history (the "time capsule")
- **Append-only `events` table** per work item: `(id, item, type, payload, at, actor)`. Event types include `created`, `question.answered`, `decision.made`, `evidence.added`, `spec.approved`, `task.exported`, `work.started`, `pr.created`, `work.paused`, `work.resumed`, `work.completed`, `imported`, `import.reverted`.
- **State = projection** of the history (e.g. "approved" = an `approved` event with no later `reopened`). Nothing can silently diverge — the structural fix for spec-kit's one-shot-pipeline problem.
- **Resume capsules:** `work.paused` bundles decisions-so-far, evidence links, open questions, next step — the lossless pickup package for you, a teammate, or a worker subagent (mattpocock handoff, persisted).
- **Time travel:** project/diff any past state; "restore" is a new revision event reusing old content (git-revert semantics, not rollback). Full snapshots only at moments that matter (approval, export).
- **Integrity:** checksummed schema migrations, doctor-style audit command, md-export modes doubling as human-readable backups, state derivable from events alone (replayability).

### 4.3 Adaptive pipeline with quality gates
Core ladder with history-enforced gates: **explore → spec → plan → tasks → export**.
- **Explore decision gate (spec-kit "assessment" insight):** the explore stage can end in **go / needs-clarification / stop** — stopping with a documented reason is a valid outcome; only `go` creates a spec.
- **Spec interview** (rpiv machinery) plays spec-kit's `clarify` role: targeted questions, answers encoded back into the spec, rerunnable per focus area.
- **Requirements checklist** (spec-kit `checklist`): reviewer-owned quality checklists ("unit tests for your requirements") generated at spec stage, tightened by the interview; **implementation is gated on checklist state** and the pipeline may not edit reviewer-owned items.
- **Cross-artifact consistency check** (spec-kit `analyze`): read-only check across spec/plan/tasks — conflicts, gaps, ambiguities; never edits; issues route back to the owning stage and re-run until clean.
- **Task decomposition** produces phase-ordered tasks (setup / foundational / per-story / polish) with **parallel-safe markers** that feed the execution scheduler.
- Gates: `spec.approved` before task breakdown; `tasks.exported` before code work; checklist before implementation.
- Adaptive depth: small changes fast-path (spec + tasks), features run the full ladder, epics additionally check/update a **project constitution** (first-class project item, evaluated at plan and convergence).

### 4.4 Epic roadmaps (spec-of-specs, adapted)
An epic decomposes into a **roadmap**: ordered slices with stable ids, intent, scope boundaries, and dependencies. Each slice runs its own full cycle; independent slices are parallelizable via worktrees. The roadmap is a store item, not a file — linked slices give traceability from epic to specs to tasks to issues.

### 4.5 Task-sink backends (six + null) & project plan
- **Adapter contract:** the full v1 surface is `createTask`, `updateStatus`, `placeInLane`, `setTags`, `readBack`; **M1 freezes the contract with the GitHub reference adapter implementing `createTask`, `placeInLane`, `readBack` plus `isConfigured`/`verify` probes** (the `updateStatus`/`setTags` surface fills in as the five ports land) — codified as TS types in `backends/contract.ts` with contract tests, freezing when GitHub passes them (M1 — see `spec-0003`).
- **v1 adapters:** `null` (store-native lanes/status/assignment), `github` (issues; issues + Projects-v2 items via GraphQL), `linear` (issues/projects/cycles, scoped API keys), `jira` (issues/boards/sprints/transitions, Basic auth), `notion` (database rows/status groups, integration token), `trello` (cards/lists/labels, key+token), `clickup` (tasks/lists/statuses, raw personal-token header).
- **Graded native parity:** each adapter maps neutral concepts to the platform's real equivalents — no fake ones. Documented per-platform mapping (lanes → milestone/project-status/sprint/status-group/list; tags → labels/multi-select; read-back → issue state/transitions/webhook-or-poll).
- **Credentials = environment variables only** (`gh` auth, `LINEAR_API_KEY`, `JIRA_HOST`+`JIRA_EMAIL`+`JIRA_TOKEN`, `NOTION_TOKEN`, `TRELLO_KEY`+`TRELLO_TOKEN`, `CLICKUP_TOKEN`); non-secret target ids live in the project plan config. Secrets never enter the repo or the store.
- **Doctor gains per-adapter checks:** credential validity, expiry warnings (Jira tokens expire 1–365 days), permission probe, target reachability, platform quirks (ClickUp raw header, Notion connection sharing).
- **Project plan** is a first-class store concept: workspace location (repo / account / org), milestone lanes (MVP, V1, V2, after-MVP, maintenance), label taxonomy, naming convention, board fields. Interviewed at cycle-planning, persisted as events, **applied idempotently at export with preview** — conventions stay consistent because they're generated, not hand-typed.
- Issue bodies carry traceability: spec excerpt, acceptance criteria, capsule/spec-version reference.
- Null sink: without any adapter, the store itself presents lanes/status/assignment (queryable board).

### 4.6 Sink onboarding (per non-GitHub adapter)
- **Trigger:** contextual (first attempt to use an unconfigured sink launches the guided flow) + explicit `/spec connect <platform>`.
- **Flow (plain language):** exact URL to create the credential, which permissions/scopes to pick, the exact env var to set — **the dev sets it in their own shell; the extension never handles secrets** — then target selection (team/project/board/database/list ids stored in the project plan) and a **read-only verification probe**.
- **GitHub is exempt:** lightweight `gh` auth + remote check.
- **Completion state:** the store marks the adapter ready/not-ready; **doctor shows a readiness matrix of all six**.

### 4.7 Execution loop (v1)
- `/spec run <task>` (or conversational equivalent) → **one or more worker subagents**, each in an isolated git worktree (worktree isolation default-on for code-changing tasks), context = task + capsule (decisions, evidence, acceptance criteria).
- **[P]-aware scheduling:** parallel-safe markers from task decomposition drive worker scheduling; per-task path ownership prevents collisions.
- **Checklist gate:** worker runs are gated on requirements-checklist state (spec-kit `implement` semantics).
- PR creation as a separate reviewed step; reviewer subagents verify; **convergence loop (spec-kit `converge`, adapted):** after execution, an append-only gap assessment — either "done" or missing work is appended as new tasks; repeat until converged. `work.completed` events flow back to store and sink.
- Humans can equally claim tasks and work normally; the store records status either way.
- **Isolation is plain git worktrees only** — specd has no GitButler backend or detection; a project using GitButler for its own git flow is unaffected (orthogonal).

## 5. Risks (all first-class, sequenced by the walking skeleton)

| Risk | Attention point | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State integrity | Append-only discipline, checksummed migrations, doctor audit, replayable projections | M0 (foundational) |
| Abstraction drift | Vendor-neutral core contract tests; no adapter may add core fields | M0 (foundational) |
| Execution blast-radius | Worktree isolation default-on, extension-owned branch naming, no direct pushes, per-task path ownership | worker milestone |
| UX polish | rpiv base, atomic transitions, render-completeness tests as milestone gates | continuous |
| Sink credential drift | Expiring tokens (Jira), user-removed-token breakage (ClickUp personal tokens), connection sharing (Notion) | doctor checks, every adapter |

## 6. Success criteria (v1)

1. A full development cycle runs end-to-end in `the reference repo` via the single command, reproducing decisions "to its current state" from scratch.
2. Team members can find and act on tasks in the configured sink; every issue traces back to its spec version via capsule references.
3. Null-sink mode is fully usable with zero external platform.
4. No grill code reused; grill's final knowledges migrate cleanly (spec-0002 acceptance).

# Implementation Plan — `specd` extension (walking skeleton)

**Scope:** all work happens inside the extension's own package (`packages/specd`) and its `.spec` data in test repos; the host repo only gains the new package directory (auto-wired by the root `packages/*/index.ts` glob). Working package/command names are placeholders (`specd`, `/spec`) pending final naming.

**Build order doctrine:** walking skeleton — prove every stage exists and connects on one tiny real change, then thicken each stage per milestone. Test bed: `the reference repo` (user-granted pnpm monorepo). Spec-kit adoptions slot into existing milestones: M1 stays the thin proof (approval gate only); M2 adds the planning gates; M3 adds the execution loop mechanics.

## M0 — Skeleton foundation ✅ (built and green)

**Deliverables**
- `packages/specd` scaffold: `index.ts` (thin registration), package manifest with `pi.extensions`, biome-conformant.
- `store/`: SQLite event-history store on `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` — items table, append-only `events` table `(id, item, type, payload, at, actor)`, links table, projection queries, checksummed schema migrations, FTS index.
- Canonical command registered (`/spec` placeholder) with store-state dashboard: reads projections, reports items and their states.
- Doctor audit: store integrity check (events derivable → projections consistent).
- Vendor-neutral core contract tests: core schema exposes only neutral concepts (lanes, tags, states, assignment).

**Acceptance criteria — all met**
1. Store opens, events append, projections query correctly; corruption/rollback of projections is detected by doctor.
2. `/spec` in a test repo shows a truthful, empty dashboard; optional verb commands registered but minimal.
3. `npm run check` (biome + tsc) and package tests pass.
4. Contract tests prove no sink-specific concepts leak into core.

## M1 — Vertical slice + reference adapter (one tiny real change on the reference repo)

**Design record:** `spec-0003` (agent-sequenced, code-gated orchestration; adapter contract; execution seam). This milestone implements it as written there.

**Schema additions (M0 store, additive to v1 — no migration):** event types `work.started`, `pr.created`.

**Deliverables**
- **Flow prompt + minimal tool set:** `specd_create_item`, `specd_append_event`, `specd_add_link`, `specd_export`, `specd_dashboard` — gates enforced in tool code (`specd_export`/`task.exported` refuse without `spec.approved`; unknown event types rejected at the boundary).
- **Stages (fast-path):** explore asks once ("unknowns worth researching?") → optional single jina query → `evidence.added`; spec interview via rpiv-ask-user-question filling the fixed template (Intent / Requirements / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope) → approval question → `spec.approved`; **plan item** (approach + `decision.made` events; no plan gate in M1); 1–3 task items with acceptance criteria + path scope.
- **GitHub reference adapter** (`backends/github.ts`, gh CLI): `createTask` (traceability body + idempotent `spec:<slug>` labels), `placeInLane` (Projects v2 `addToProject` + status via GraphQL), `readBack` (`gh issue view` on dashboard refresh), `isConfigured`/`verify` probes. **Null sink implements `createTask` natively.**
- **`backends/contract.ts`:** adapter contract types + contract tests — **FROZEN when GitHub passes them**.
- **Targeting:** first export asks project/lane via rpiv; persisted in store `meta`; reused thereafter (formal onboarding = M2).
- **Execution seam:** `/spec run <task>` → `work.started` → **one** pi-subagents worker in a **plain git worktree (no GitButler anywhere in specd)** with context = task + acceptance criteria + path scope + branch `specd/<task-id>-<slug>` + capsule → implement/commit/push → `gh pr create` → `pr.created` → worker self-check → `work.completed`.
- **Capsule:** explicit pause (conversational or `/spec pause`) writes `work.paused` (decisions, open questions, evidence, next step); dashboard shows paused state; resume reads it back.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. One tiny real change in the reference repo runs end-to-end: explore (ask-once) → spec (template, approved) → plan item → task → 1 GitHub issue (traceable body + labels) → project item → 1 worker in 1 worktree → 1 PR → status events back in store and issue state.
2. Every artifact traces: issue body references spec version + capsule; events replay to reconstruct state.
3. Gate enforcement demonstrable in code: `specd_export` refuses an unapproved spec.
4. Adapter contract frozen: contract tests pass for `github` + `null`; `placeInLane` and `readBack` demonstrated at least once each.
5. A paused and resumed cycle resumes losslessly from the capsule.
6. Worker blast-radius holds: own branch only, never `main`, no force-push, path scope respected.
7. `npm run check` + tests green, including the new contract tests.

## M2 — Thicken planning + five adapter ports + migration + onboarding

**Deliverables**
- Adaptive depth: fast-path (spec+tasks) vs full ladder vs epic+roadmap, sized by the flow.
- **Spec-kit planning gates:** explore decision gate (go / needs-clarification / stop); requirements checklist (reviewer-owned, created at spec, tightened by the interview); read-only cross-artifact consistency check with fix-at-source re-run loop; task phases (setup/foundational/story/polish) + parallel-safe markers in the task schema; epic roadmap concept (ordered slices, dependencies, per-slice specs); constitution as a first-class project item checked at plan.
- **Project plan concept**: workspace location (repo/account/org), lanes (MVP/V1/V2/after-MVP/maintenance), label taxonomy, naming convention, board fields — interviewed at cycle-planning, applied idempotently at export with preview.
- **Five adapter ports against the frozen contract** with graded native parity: Linear (GraphQL, scoped keys), Jira (REST v3, Basic auth), Notion (database rows, integration token), Trello (cards/lists, key+token), ClickUp (tasks/lists/statuses, raw `pk_` header). Contract test suite passes identically for all six.
- **Three storage modes** (db-only / db+md in-repo / db+md in separate repo or folder) with md promotion.
- **Grill migration** per `spec-0002`: preview-first, snapshot-default profile (full-history + curated opt-in), hybrid type mapping, graph-preserving provenance events + relation table, atomic single-transaction runs with batch id, idempotent origin-id tracking, link-safe ordering, md regeneration via overlay, merge-with-flags, post-import audit.
- **Sink onboarding** per design §4.6: contextual trigger + `/spec connect <platform>` for the five non-GitHub sinks (plain-language steps, exact credential URLs/scopes, dev-owned env vars, target selection, read-only verification probe); GitHub lightweight check; doctor readiness matrix of all six.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Depth adaptation demonstrable on three differently-sized the reference repo changes.
2. The explore decision gate demonstrably stops with a documented reason when the answer is "not yet"; only `go` creates a spec.
3. Requirements checklist and consistency check demonstrably block progression on failures and re-run clean after fixes at the owning stage.
4. Project plan applies idempotently (re-run = no drift), with preview before apply; lanes/labels/naming consistent and searchable.
5. All six adapters pass the identical contract test suite; graded-parity mapping documented per platform (what each maps and what it lacks).
6. All three storage modes pass the same test suite against one schema.
7. Migration: the reference repo's final knowledges import via the snapshot profile; audit passes (counts, checksums, doctor, idempotent re-run); a batch revert restores the exact pre-import projection; merge into a non-empty store flags duplicates without touching native items.
8. Onboarding: each non-GitHub sink completable from the guided flow alone; doctor readiness matrix reflects per-adapter state; no secret ever enters the repo or store.

## M3 — Thicken execution

**Deliverables**
- Parallel workers across worktrees with per-task path ownership and extension-owned branch naming; **[P]-aware scheduling** from task-phase parallel markers.
- **Checklist-gated worker runs** (spec-kit `implement` semantics): implementation blocked while reviewer-owned checklist items are unchecked.
- Reviewer subagents on completion; PR creation as reviewed step (no direct pushes to protected refs).
- **Convergence loop** (spec-kit `converge`, adapted): append-only gap assessment after execution — "done" or missing work appended as new tasks; repeat until converged.
- Status flow-back to store and sink; conflict policy across worktrees.

**Acceptance criteria**
1. Two non-conflicting tasks execute concurrently in separate worktrees, both PRs created, both statuses recorded; a path-ownership collision is detected and serialized, not corrupted.
2. Reviewer findings route back as events; failing review blocks task completion.
3. Convergence loop demonstrably appends missing work and reports "done" only when gaps are closed.
4. Blast-radius rules hold: workers never push directly, branch naming is convention-owned, checklist gate blocks premature implementation.

## M4 — Full the reference repo cycle replay

**Deliverables**
- Full development-cycle replay in the reference repo "from scratch to its current state" through the extension, using migrated knowledge as reference material.

**Acceptance criteria (maps to design success criteria)**
1. End-to-end cycle via the single command; decisions reproduced to current state.
2. Tasks findable/actuable in the configured sink; issues trace to spec versions via capsules.
3. Null-sink mode fully usable with zero external platform.
4. Grill migration clean (no code reuse anywhere in the package); migrated knowledge is searchable and correctly linked.
5. UX bar met: rpiv-level responsiveness; no half-rendered states at any milestone.
6. All six adapters contract-tested; doctor readiness matrix green for configured sinks.

## Validation doctrine
- Pure logic unit-tested per house pattern (grill's colocated-test discipline, reimplemented).
- Every milestone runs against the real the reference repo repo, not fixtures only.
- UX gates precede feature gates within each milestone (render-completeness before new capability).
- The adapter contract test suite is the single standard for all six sinks — a port is done when it passes the same tests GitHub passed.","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Migration Design — grill → specd knowledge transfer

**Scope:** the `migrate/` module of `packages/specd` and its interaction with the `.spec` store. Companion to the main design (`spec-0001`); planned in milestone M2 of `plan-0001`.

## 1. Purpose

Move knowledge created by the grill extension into specd format so grill can retire without stranding knowledge. Driving case: `the reference repo` — migrate the **final knowledges of the project's current state**. Generalized so most devs get what they need via profiles.

**Clean-room rule:** specd reads grill's `atoms.db` as a foreign schema (data only) and reimplements all logic. Grill is never modified.

## 2. Source surface (what grill's store contains)

`.pi/knowledge/atoms.db` — SQLite v2 (`meta.schema_version` guard, WAL, FTS): **12 atom types** (decision, research, plan, spec, task, session, validation, content, release, requirement, concept, spike), **4 statuses** (draft/accepted/promoted/superseded), **7 edge kinds** (supersedes, refined-by, depends-on, produced-by, cited, promoted-to, part-of), bodies in-db, `scope`, `sources`, promotion machinery writing md into the repo tree. Precedent: grill's own one-shot legacy converter (`atom/migrate.ts`, never auto-reads unknown versions).

## 3. Migration profiles

| Profile | What transfers | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **snapshot** (default) | Final knowledges of the current state: non-superseded atoms, current statuses, current promotion state | ✅ |
| **full-history** | Everything, including superseded chains (preserved as linked items) | opt-in |
| **curated** | Chosen types / scopes / atoms per run; selections recorded for determinism | opt-in |

Sessions, settings, and interview transcripts never transfer — process artifacts, not knowledge.

## 4. Type mapping (hybrid)

- **Direct to active items** (a mid-flight project keeps working specs/tasks immediately):
  - grill `spec` → specd spec
  - grill `task` → specd task
  - grill `requirement` → requirement within its spec
- **Knowledge items** (first-class item type, linkable into cycles later): decision, research, plan, validation, concept, spike, content, release — carrying origin metadata: `originType`, `originId`, `grillStatus`, `scope`, `sources`.

## 5. Event & relation mapping (graph-preserving)

- **One `imported` event per item**; payload = the complete grill record (grillId, type, title, body, status, scope, sources, createdAt) as provenance. `at` = migration run time; `actor` = migration. **No fabricated timelines** — grill never recorded per-atom status history.
- **Generic relation table** preserves all 7 edge kinds: supersedes, refined-by, depends-on, produced-by, cited, part-of survive as links; `promoted-to` becomes md-overlay pointer metadata rather than a graph edge.
- Superseded chains survive as linked knowledge items in the full-history profile.

## 6. Mechanics

1. **Preview first** (always, plain language): counts per type, what becomes active, what markdown will be written, flagged overlaps/duplicates. Requires confirmation.
2. **Atomic run:** each import executes as **one SQLite transaction** — a failure at item 137 of 200 leaves nothing behind; re-running starts clean.
3. **Batch id:** every run stamps a batch id on its items (and records the source store path).
4. **Idempotent:** items tracked by grill origin id; re-runs skip already-imported items or refresh them if the source changed.
5. **Link-safe ordering:** imports are ordered so relations never dangle (topological over supersedes/dependencies).
6. **Markdown regeneration:** promoted atoms regenerate their md exports through specd's promotion overlay in storage modes 2 (in-repo) and 3 (external store/folder); demotion removes them.

## 7. Failure & rollback story

- **Partial failure:** impossible to half-land — the transaction boundary guarantees all-or-nothing.
- **Undo a wrong import:** one compensating `import.reverted` event naming the batch; projections exclude the batch; md files the import wrote are removed. History stays append-only — the revert is itself an event.
- **Non-empty target store:** merges by origin-id (idempotent); the preview **flags suspicious title duplicates**; native specd items are never touched or overwritten.
- **Grill's existing promoted md files** in the repo tree: left untouched (grill is never modified); the preview flags path overlaps with specd's overlay output and offers optional cleanup with explicit confirmation.
- **Multiple grill stores/workspaces:** one migration run per store path; each batch records its source.

## 8. Search continuity

Imported titles/bodies are indexed in specd's FTS index (node:sqlite, grill precedent) and the index is rebuilt on import, so migrated knowledge is searchable immediately.

## 9. Validation & acceptance

- Post-import audit: item counts match the source per type, per-item content checksums, doctor projection check (state derivable from events), re-run idempotency produces an identical store state.
- Hard failures (no auto-recovery): missing/unreadable source, `schema_version` mismatch, corrupt source — surfaced in plain language with next-step guidance.
- Acceptance (M2): grill atoms + edges import as `imported` events with links intact; snapshot profile migrates the reference repo's final knowledges; revert of a batch restores the pre-import projection state exactly.

## 10. Terminology

User-facing wording stays plain and business-general: "import your existing knowledge", "connections", "current state", "undo this import" — never "event sourcing", "projections", "relation tables". Technical vocabulary lives in maintainer docs only.","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# M1 Detailed Design — Vertical Slice + GitHub Reference Adapter

**Scope:** the M1 milestone of `plan-0001`, implementing the architecture in `spec-0001`. M0 (store, events, links, projections, doctor, contract tests) is built and green. This record captures the nine design decisions reviewed and approved before implementation.

## 1. Orchestration model — agent-sequenced, code-gated

The pipeline is **not** a programmatic controller. specd registers a minimal tool set plus a flow prompt; the interactive agent sequences the stages conversationally, and **the store decides legality**:

- Tools: `specd_create_item`, `specd_append_event`, `specd_add_link`, `specd_export`, `specd_dashboard`.
- Gates are enforced in tool code, not prompt trust: `specd_append_event('task.exported')` and `specd_export` **refuse** when no `spec.approved` event exists for the linked spec; unknown event types are rejected at the append boundary (M0 behavior).
- Elicitation runs through **rpiv-ask-user-question**; execution runs through **pi-subagents**; the sink adapter runs behind `specd_export`.

This is the house pattern (grill works exactly this way): conversational flexibility up top, structural integrity underneath.

## 2. Flow stages (fast-path)

1. **Explore — ask once:** "any unknowns worth researching first?" Yes → one jina query, findings stored as `evidence.added` events linked to the item. No → straight to the spec interview. (Adaptive depth tuning is M2.)
2. **Spec:** rpiv-driven interview fills a fixed template — **Intent / Requirements (numbered, testable) / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope** — then an approval question; approval writes `spec.approved`. **No checklist artifact in M1** (M2 adds the requirements-quality gate).
3. **Plan:** a **plan item from day one** even on fast-path — approach paragraph plus `decision.made` events linked to the plan and spec. The plan carries **no gate of its own in M1**; task creation remains gated on `spec.approved`.
4. **Tasks:** **1–3 task items**, each with title, acceptance criteria, and a **path scope** string (stored now; enforced by parallel workers in M3).

## 3. GitHub reference adapter (contract freeze)

`backends/github.ts`, implemented through the **gh CLI** (child_process spawn; gh is already authenticated):

| Capability | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| `isConfigured` / `verify` | gh auth status, remote detection, project reachability (read-only probes) |
| `createTask` | `gh issue create` — traceability body (spec excerpt, acceptance criteria, spec-version ref) + idempotent `spec:<slug>` labels |
| `placeInLane` | Projects v2 `addToProject` + status field via GraphQL, from configured project/lane |
| `readBack` | `gh issue view` state mapping, invoked on `/spec` dashboard refresh (no webhooks in M1) |

**Contract:** types live in `backends/contract.ts` with contract tests; **the contract freezes when GitHub passes them.** The **null sink** implements `createTask` natively (task status flips to `exported`, ref = itself), proving the vendor-neutral floor.

## 4. Targeting (before formal onboarding)

First export in a repo asks interactively via rpiv — which project, which lane — and the answers persist in the store's `meta` table, reused for every later export. M2 replaces this with the full onboarding + project-plan interviewing; M1 does not design onboarding twice.

## 5. Execution seam

`/spec run <task>` flow:

1. Store: `work.started` event (new event type).
2. Spawn **one** pi-subagents `worker` with **worktree isolation (plain git worktrees — no GitButler anywhere in specd)**; worker context = task + acceptance criteria + path scope + branch name + capsule.
3. Worker: implement → commit to its branch → push → `gh pr create`.
4. Store: `pr.created` event (new event type; payload: url, branch).
5. Worker self-check against acceptance criteria → pass writes `work.completed`.

**Branch naming (extension-owned):** `specd/<task-id>-<slug>` (e.g. `specd/task-0001-add-login-route`).
**Worker rules:** own branch only; never `main`; no force-push; stay inside path scope.
Both new event types are **additive to schema v1 before release** — no migration needed.

## 6. Definition of done (M1)

`work.completed` = **PR opened + worker self-check passed.** Merging is the human's call (the dev-team finish line). Reviewer agents and the append-only convergence loop arrive in M3 — M1's done is deliberately shallow.

## 7. Resume capsule

Explicit pause only (conversational "pause this" or `/spec pause`): a `work.paused` event bundling decisions-so-far, open questions, evidence links, and the next step. The dashboard shows a paused state with the capsule available; resuming reads it back. Automatic capture on session end is M2+.

## 8. Explicitly NOT in M1

Requirements-checklist gate · cross-artifact consistency check · convergence loop · reviewer subagents · webhooks · formal sink onboarding · project-plan interviewing · parallel workers / path-ownership enforcement · GitButler support · adaptive-depth tuning. Each lands in M2/M3 per `plan-0001`.

## 9. Acceptance summary

One tiny real the reference repo change travels explore → spec (approved) → plan item → task → GitHub issue (traceable, labeled) → project item → one worktree worker → PR → status events back. Gates refuse illegal transitions in code. Contract tests pass for `github` + `null`. Pause/resume is lossless.","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Not-onboarded sinks are treated as an empty kanban

**Decision.** A sink adapter (existing or future M2c port) must treat a not-onboarded workspace — one with no board structure (no status field, no lists, no labels) — as an *empty kanban*: the project-plan apply bootstraps the missing structure itself and never refuses with "set it up in the web UI first".

**Rationale.** Not all sinks ship with a kanban (Notion databases, ClickUp spaces, fresh Linear teams), and users testing or migrating between adapters (github → linear → …) hit a blank workspace every time. Requiring manual web-UI setup breaks the guided onboarding flow (design §4.6) and the "completable from the flow alone" acceptance criterion.

**Applied.**
- `backends/contract.ts`: `previewPlan`/`ensurePlan` docs now state the empty-kanban rule — contract tests for all six adapters will enforce it (M2c).
- `backends/github.ts` (reference adapter): `ensurePlan` no longer throws on a missing Status field; it creates the field via `createProjectV2Field` with the plan lanes as options. `previewPlan` reports the same as a previewable change.

**Consequence for M2c ports:** every adapter's `ensurePlan` must create its lane equivalent (workflow state, board column, status property, list, list status) on an empty workspace, and its `previewPlan` must report that as a change.

**Refined by dec-0012 (2026-10-25):** lanes are workflow columns (Model B) — the bootstrap covers workflow options for lanes + labels; status options are never created from lanes, and milestones are user-owned.","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Sink credentials: env vars first, then ~/.pi/agent/auth.json

**Decision.** specd resolves sink credentials in priority order: (1) dev-owned env vars per the onboarding registry, (2) a per-sink section in `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` (`auth.linear.key`, `auth.jira.{host,email,key}`, …) with `$VAR` indirection — the exact pattern the jina package uses for `JINA_API_KEY`. Credentials are never stored in a repo, a specd store, or a session transcript.

**Rationale.** Env-var-only onboarding forces a pi restart mid-flow and redoes setup per sandbox. The auth.json file is outside every repo, read fresh at each probe (no restart), shared across sandboxes — so testing or migrating **between adapters** (the M2c graded-parity matrix) never re-does credential setup.

**Applied.** `backends/onboarding.ts` (`resolveSinkCredentials` + `probeSink` + readiness matrix consumed by `/spec doctor`), onboarding steps in `/spec connect <sink>`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` honored so tests inject a temp agent dir.","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Research — sink adapter contracts for the five M2c ports

Findings verified against official API docs (sources below). Maps each platform onto the frozen `SinkAdapter` contract (`packages/specd/backends/contract.ts`): `isConfigured`/`verify` probes, `createTask(TaskExport) → {externalRef, url}`, `readBack(externalRef) → {state}`, `placeInLane(externalRef, lane)`, `setTags(externalRef, tags)`, `updateStatus(externalRef, state)`, `previewPlan`/`ensurePlan` (empty-kanban bootstrap per dec-0010).

## Linear — GraphQL, single endpoint
- `POST https://api.linear.app/graphql`; auth header **`Authorization: <API_KEY>` — NO `Bearer`** for API keys (Bearer is OAuth-only; wrong header = UNAUTHENTICATED). Errors come back HTTP 200 + `errors[]` — always check `errors` before `data`.
- `createTask`: mutation `issueCreate(input: { teamId, title, description /* markdown */, labelIds, stateId? })` → `issue { id, identifier (e.g. ENG-123), url }`. externalRef = `identifier`; url returned directly.
- `placeInLane`/`updateStatus`: query team `workflowStates` (id per state name) → `issueUpdate(id: "ENG-123", input: { stateId })` — identifier works as issue id.
- `setTags`: `issueLabelCreate` per label (team-scoped), then `labelIds` on create/update.
- `readBack`: `issue(id) { state { name }, completedAt }` → state open/closed mapping.
- Workspace coords (sink setup): `teamId`. ensurePlan CAN bootstrap labels + (custom) workflow states via GraphQL mutations — full empty-kanban parity.
- Rate limits: ~5000 req/h/user + complexity budget; prefer small queries.
- Doctor quirk: key inherits the creating user's permissions (user-scoped, long-lived).

## Jira — REST v3, Basic auth
- `https://<site>/rest/api/3/...`; auth `Authorization: Basic base64(email:api_token)`. Token lifetime is **1–365 days** (doctor expiry check required — design §4.5).
- `createTask`: `POST /rest/api/3/issue` body `fields: { project: {key}, issuetype: {id|name}, summary, labels: [string...], description: <ADF doc> }`. **description is Atlassian Document Format** (`{type:"doc",version:1,content:[paragraph…]}`) — the one real converter needed. Response `{id, key}` → externalRef = `key` (e.g. ED-24); public url = `<site>/browse/<key>`.
- **Decision (default): minimal markdown→ADF** — line-based: `# heading` → heading block, `- item` → bulletList items, everything else → paragraph per line, inline markdown stripped to plain text. Upgrade only if bodies need richer fidelity.
- `placeInLane`/`updateStatus`: board columns = workflow statuses; `GET /issue/{key}/transitions` → `POST /issue/{key}/transitions {transition: {id}}`. Lane→transition mapping resolved per project at plan time.
- `setTags`: labels are free-form strings on the issue — no ensure needed; `PUT /issue/{key} {labels: [...]}` replaces the set (read-modify-write).
- `readBack`: `GET /issue/{key}?fields=status` → `fields.status.name`; state category (done/in-progress/todo) available via `status.statusCategory`.
- ensurePlan: labels need no bootstrap; **creating statuses/columns is project-admin work** (company-managed boards) — ensurePlan reports missing lanes as "create in Jira UI" (honest gap) unless a team-managed project API path is verified live.
- Scopes (classic): `read:jira-work`, `write:jira-work`.

## Notion — integration token, database rows
- `https://api.notion.com/v1/...`; auth `Authorization: Bearer <token>` + `Notion-Version: 2022-06-28` header. Integration must have the target database **shared with it** (connection sharing — onboarding step; the classic failure mode is empty query results).
- `createTask`: `POST /v1/pages` `{parent: {database_id}, properties: {Name: {title:[{text:{content}}]}, Status: {status:{name}}, Tags: {multi_select:[{name}]}}}`. Body content = children blocks (paragraph blocks) — markdown degrades to paragraphs. externalRef = page id; url returned.
- `placeInLane`/`updateStatus`: `PATCH /v1/pages/{id}` property by name.
- `readBack`: `GET /v1/pages/{id}` → `properties.<status>.status.name`.
- **Status options ARE API-writable now** (the 2023 StackOverflow answer is outdated): `PATCH /v1/databases/{id}` `properties.<name>.status.options` = complete retained list, new options accept `group` (To-do/In progress/Complete); select/multi-select options follow the same rules. Group definitions themselves stay UI-managed. So ensurePlan CAN bootstrap lanes + tags — near-full empty-kanban parity.
- Decision (default): use the legacy database endpoints pinned to version 2022-06-28 for v1 (the newer "data source" endpoints are a rename layer; migrate later if needed).
- Rate limits: ~3 req/s average.

## Trello — key + token, plain REST
- `https://api.trello.com/1/...`; auth `key` + `token` query params on every call.
- `createTask`: `POST /1/cards` `idList, name, desc (markdown supported), idLabels` → externalRef = card id; url = card `shortUrl`/`url`.
- `placeInLane`/`updateStatus`: lanes = **lists**; `PUT /1/cards/{id} {idList}`. readBack = `GET /1/cards/{id}/list` → list name (membership-as-state; no native open/closed per card — `closed` means archived).
- `setTags`: labels are board-scoped with name+color; `PUT /1/cards/{id} {idLabels}` (replace set).
- ensurePlan: full bootstrap — `POST /1/lists {name, idBoard}` for lanes, `POST /1/boards/{id}/labels` for tags. Complete empty-kanban parity; workspace coords = board id.

## ClickUp — raw personal-token header
- `https://api.clickup.com/api/v2/...`; auth header **`Authorization: pk_...` raw (no Bearer)** — confirmed in the official OpenAPI description. Docs are agent-friendly (`.../reference/<page>.md`, index at `/llms.txt`).
- `createTask`: `POST /v2/list/{list_id}/task` `{name (required), markdown_content (markdown description — preferred over `description`), status (existing status name), tags: [names], assignees}` → externalRef = task id; url = `https://app.clickup.com/t/<team_id>/<task_id>`.
- `placeInLane`/`updateStatus`: `PUT /v2/task/{task_id} {status}`; available statuses come from the list (GET task/list status).
- `setTags`: tags are **space-level** — `POST /v2/team/{team_id}/tag {name}` to ensure, `POST /v2/task/{task_id}/tag/{tag_name}` to attach (create-task also accepts `tags` names).
- **ensurePlan gap: no v2 endpoint creates list statuses** — missing lanes are reported as "create in ClickUp UI" (honest parity gap); labels/tags bootstrap fine. Workspace coords: `team_id` + `space_id` + `list_id`.
- Doctor quirk: personal tokens die silently when the user revokes/removes them — verify() should fail with a re-onboarding hint (design §4.5 risk).

## Cross-adapter decisions recorded
1. **externalRef conventions**: Linear=identifier, Jira=key, Notion=page id, Trello=card id, ClickUp=task id (+ team_id for custom ids). `TaskCreated.url` always the human-readable URL.
2. **Body format ladder**: markdown native (Linear, Trello, ClickUp via markdown_content) → paragraph degradation (Notion children blocks) → minimal ADF writer (Jira only).
3. **State model**: readBack maps platform state → `{open|closed}` neutral state (github parity); placeInLane maps plan lanes to the platform's lane equivalent.
4. **Empty-kanban grading**: Trello/Linear/Notion can fully bootstrap structure; Jira/ClickUp report UI-required gaps in previewPlan and never fail silently.
5. **Env var naming** stays as shipped in the onboarding registry (`JIRA_API_TOKEN`/`NOTION_API_TOKEN`/`CLICKUP_API_TOKEN`, `TRELLO_KEY`+`TRELLO_TOKEN`, `LINEAR_API_KEY`) — auth.json sections are keyed by sink id so naming is internally consistent; the design's older names (`JIRA_TOKEN`, `NOTION_TOKEN`, `CLICKUP_TOKEN`) are superseded by the registry.

## Sources
- https://linear.app/developers/graphql (endpoint, auth, issueCreate/issueUpdate, workflowStates)
- https://unified.to/blog/linear_api_key_how_to_generate_and_use_it_graphql_guide_for_developers (no-Bearer trap, rate limits)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/intro/ (auth modes, ADF scope, pagination)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issues/ (create issue body incl. labels/ADF description, transitions)
- https://developers.notion.com/reference/update-property-schema-object + /reference/property-object (select/multi-select/status options writable, groups, title id)
- https://developers.notion.com/reference/update-a-database (PATCH database, headers)
- https://developer.clickup.com/reference/createtask.md (OpenAPI: raw pk_ header, name/description/markdown_content/tags/status)
- https://developer.clickup.com/reference/gettasks (list endpoint, markdown param)
- https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/trello/rest/api-group-cards/ (cards/list endpoints surface)","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Route — integration → reset → fresh pre-dev simulation → migration validation

**Context.** The specd extension is feature-complete (store, gates, adapters ×6, execution seam, scheduling, storage modes, onboarding, importer — 133 tests green). This route codifies the agreed phase order and mechanics (decisions D1–D13 + the naming decision dec-0013 + the workflow-lanes decision dec-0012 from the grill + live sessions).

**Global constraints.**
- The extension's host repo is public: everything committed there stays generic — no sandbox-specific names, paths, or knowledge. All sandbox work lives in the user's private sandbox repos.
- One thing at a time: each leg is settled and validated before the next.
- Phase artifacts: P1 = throwaway; P3 = keep-worthy (the real beginning).

## Status
- **P0 — KB scrub: DONE.** All sandbox identifiers genericized in the host-repo KB (10 atoms).
- **P1 — Integration: DONE, fully green.** null mini-cycle (gates + export); reset script built (`scripts/reset-specd.sh`, full local sweep + session-export sweep + external-artifact report, idempotent); github mini-cycle on the throwaway board (issue + lane + statusMap landing verified live); review loop verified (failed review → fix → re-review → PR → work.completed); PR #2 merged (README + smoke script — the repo's first real content).
- **P2 — Restart: DONE** (the script's first real job ran clean; the merged content survives on main).
- **P3 — Fresh pre-dev simulation: DONE (playtest report + QA pass).** Epic → roadmap (4 ordered slices, depends-on chain) → slice-1 pipeline (spec approved → plan with 5 decisions + constitution anchored → 3 tasks with conventional types, 2×[P] → exported null ×3). Negative probes: unknown-cycle refusal, double-export refusal. Live catches fixed same-run: ladder directionality (9e9d634), scheduler direction + `specd_remove_link` (2189402). Sealed-run deviation disclosed in the play report (owner-directed reference read lifted the seal for constraint detail; structure/tasks derived fresh).
- **P4 — Migration validation: remaining (last phase).** Temp copy of the reference knowledge store → preview → apply → full audit (counts, doctor, idempotent re-run, revert) → delete. Disposable temp repo skeleton next to the originals; originals untouched.

## Post-route
- **Worksets design (first post-route feature)** — from route evidence; local OpenSpec forks copy as reference; driving use case: knowledge repo + code repo together for implementation sessions.
- **Deferred:** five-adapter live order + credentials (agent decides, one at a time); sink-side "done" mapping refinements; convergence loop live exercise (rides the first real slice cycles).","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

- [ ] Spec created only via the cycle gate; approval is an explicit user yes.
- [ ] NEGATIVE: `specd_export` refuses while the spec is unapproved (plain-language reason).
- [ ] After approval: plan linked, 1–2 tasks created with path scopes, export with sink=null succeeds.
- [ ] Dashboard shows exported tasks store-native; event history reconstructs every state (doctor clean).

## P1.b — reset script

- [ ] After a run: `.spec/store.db` (+WAL/SHM) gone; next store open re-inits fresh (doctor reports an empty healthy store).
- [ ] Local md mirrors (docs/specd/*.md) removed when present.
- [ ] `git worktree list` shows no specd/* worktrees afterwards; specd/* branches pruned.
- [ ] Script prints the external-artifact report (GitHub issues/PRs, test project) it cannot touch.

- [ ] Reviewer subagent produced findings; passing verdict recorded; PR created from the worktree branch afterwards.
- [ ] `pr.created` + `work.completed` recorded; read-back sync reflects the state on the dashboard.

# Workflow lanes model (Model B) — lanes are the board's workflow columns

**Decision.** specd "lanes" map onto the sink's WORKFLOW columns (GitHub Status options, Trello lists, Notion status property, ClickUp statuses, Linear workflow states). The default lane taxonomy is the workflow set — Backlog, Ready, In progress, In review, Done, Blocked (taken from the reference project template). **Milestones/sprints are the developer's own grouping on top** (each milestone runs through the same lanes, agile/scrum style); the developer manages milestone target dates — specd never writes milestones.

**Supersedes.** The interim milestone mapping direction (lanes → Milestone field, considered 2026-10-25) — rejected after grounding on the reference project: its Status field is pure workflow (Backlog/Ready/In progress/In review/Done/Blocked) and polluting it with phase names (MVP/after-MVP) was the original complaint. Milestone option-pollution on the test board was cleaned up (Status restored to Todo/In Progress/Done).

**Mechanics (D15 kept + extended).**
- `SinkSetup.statusMap`: explicit specd item status → board workflow option (e.g. exported→Ready, in-progress→In progress, done→Done). `updateStatus` writes exactly the mapped option; unmapped states pass through as the option name and fail with the available list if absent. `previewPlan` verifies statusMap targets — status options are the board's own workflow and are **never created from lanes**.
- `placeInLane(lane)` = set the workflow column (the lane IS the Status option).
- `createTask` lands the issue on the board in the mapped `exported` state.
- `DEFAULT_LANES` = Backlog, Ready, In progress, In review, Done, Blocked.

**Views (display layer, graded parity).** GitHub: `createProjectV2View(projectId, name, layout BOARD_LAYOUT/TABLE_LAYOUT/ROADMAP_LAYOUT, configuration?)` — offerable as display scaffolding in ensurePlan later. Linear: custom views (likely `viewCreate` — verify at port). ClickUp: view endpoints exist (partial). Notion/Trello: not API-exposed — graded gaps. Views are never load-bearing: items do not live "in" views.

**Provenance.** Found live in the P1.c integration run (user rejected MVP/after-MVP as Status options; reference project #3 = the GitHub project template as the ideal shape).","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

type=decision
original_id=dec-0013
original_status=draft

# Naming conventions — conventional commits everywhere

**Decision.** Every artifact's name states the goal of the operation, aligned with conventional commits: task items carry an optional conventional type (feat | fix | chore | docs | test | refactor | perf | style | build | ci) in their created payload (`specd_create_item` extra, default feat); scope derives from the task's path scope (first non-generic directory segment — files at the root and pure-glob scopes give none).

**The scheme.**
- Branch: `specd/<type>/<ref>-<slug>` (e.g. `specd/feat/task-0001-add-login-route`)
- Issue/PR title: `type(scope): Title` / `type: Title` (subject starts lowercase; acronyms survive)
- Commits: `type(scope): subject` — mandated in the worker brief
- Descriptions: bodies keep goal traceability (spec ref + acceptance criteria)

**The specd/ prefix stays.** It is the tool's branch namespace — same legitimacy as dependabot/renovate prefixes — and the reset sweep prunes `specd/*` by it. Configurable later only if a real need appears. Rejected alternative: putting the store ref in every title (`[task-0001]` suffix) — noisier; the ref lives in labels + body (traceability unchanged).

**Mechanics.** `naming.ts` (pure, tested): ccTypeOf reads the created payload's type; scopeOf derives from path scope; ccTitle/branchName compose. `specd_create_worktree` uses branchName; `specd_export` supports `{type}/{scope}` placeholders in the naming template with DEFAULT_NAMING = `{type}({scope}): {title}`; RUN_PROMPT mandates the conventions in the worker brief.

**Provenance.** User DX request during the route execution (after the first live PR: naming should honor the goal of each operation).","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}

# Review — specd against the original idea sources

Sources reviewed (fetched 2026-10-25/26): spec-kit concepts (sdd, spec-persistence, spec-of-specs, complex-features), guides (agentic-sdlc, evolving-specs, quickstart, customization), and OpenSpec docs (stores-beta, worksets). Verdict per source: what it prescribes → what specd does → status.

## 1. spec-kit — What is SDD?
- **Intent-driven (what before how)** → spec stage gated before plan/tasks. ✅
- **Guardrailed spec creation** → gates enforced in code (store-state refusals), stronger than prompt compliance. ✅
- **Multi-step refinement** → staged pipeline + revision/reopen events. ✅
- **Phases**: greenfield ✅ (fast-path) · brownfield ✅ (adoption loop + migration) · **creative exploration (parallel implementations) — deferred** (v1 non-goal per design).
- **Persistence non-prescription** → specd deliberately answers it (see #4).

## 2. spec-kit — Quickstart (specify → plan → tasks → implement)
- Mapped 1:1: `/spec start` → spec → plan → tasks → export → run. ✅
- specd additions: explore stage before specify, explicit approval gate, sink export, convergence command.

## 3. spec-kit — Agentic SDLC
- Agent-sequenced SDLC with human decisions at handoffs → the whole specd architecture (agent drives, tools refuse illegal transitions). ✅
- Assess workflow with **go / needs-clarification / kill** verdicts → specd explore gate: **go / needs-clarification / stop**. ✅ (same vocabulary, stop ≈ kill)
- Dogfooding (spec-kit used itself for the bundler) → **specd just did the same**: P3 built lingua-lair-core's own epic/roadmap/slices with specd. ✅
- Label-triggered repo-workflow intake (feature-assess on GitHub Actions) → not built; the explore stage covers it interactively. Deferred.

## 4. spec-kit — Spec Persistence Models (the central differentiator)
Spec Kit names three post-delivery models as team conventions: **flow-back**, **flow-forward**, **living spec** (plus the temporal frame: spec-first / spec-anchored / spec-as-source). It prescribes none.
- **specd SUBSUMES all three by construction**: the append-only event history is immutable (flow-forward audit ✓), the projection is the living contract (living ✓ — revisions via body.updated), discoveries enter as evidence/decision events and replay into state (flow-back ✓ without silent-drift risk — replay IS the reconciliation check, doctor verifies it).
- No team convention needed; nothing to choose, nothing to drift. This was the design's answer to spec-kit's open question — built and verified (P1/P3 replays, doctor audits).

## 5. spec-kit — Evolving Specs (brownfield loops)
- Delivery loop `specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge` (converge append-only, adds remaining tasks) → `/spec` pipeline + `/spec converge`. ✅ built (live exercise pending first real slice).
- Analyze reports without editing → `/spec analyze` + `specd_consistency`. ✅
- Constitution governance → constitution item anchored to plans (consistency-checked). ✅

## 6. spec-kit — Customization (extensions, presets, bundles, workflows, project-local overrides)
- Not built in v1 — accepted design non-goal (process customization/presets post-v1). specd itself demonstrates the "extension" building block at the pi layer. Deferred.

## 7. spec-kit — Complex Features (context exhaustion)
Four options for keeping implement runs inside context limits:
- **Option 2 (sub-agent delegation)** → BUILT as the default architecture: per-task worker subagents in isolated worktrees with focused context.
- **Option 4 (decompose into smaller specs)** → BUILT first-class: the epic/roadmap ladder with consistency rules (vs spec-kit's manual file convention + community extension).
- **Option 1 (limit tasks per run) / Option 3 (combine)** → superseded structurally: `/spec run <task>` is task-scoped by design and waves schedule parallelism — the mitigation is unnecessary, not missing.
- Verdict: adopted with structural improvement — specd's shape makes the workarounds native.

## 8. spec-kit — Spec of Specs
- Roadmap pass → roadmap artifact → ordered slices with back-references and depends-on. Spec Kit: manual markdown convention + optional community extension.
- **specd: first-class** — epic/roadmap items, slice specs, depends-on ordering, consistency rules (missing roadmap / missing slices / non-spec slices / unordered), live-verified in P3 (after the directionality fix). ✅

## 9. OpenSpec — Stores (beta)
- Standalone planning repos with identity, machine-local registry, root resolution, read-only **references**.
- specd: the `.spec` store is already standalone-per-repo and sink-portable (P4 migration audit passed on a copy). ✅ for the core idea.
- Registry / root resolution / cross-repo references → **not built — D11** (first post-route feature). Migration import makes old knowledge portable, which covers the brownfield half.

## 10. OpenSpec — Worksets (beta)
- Personal, per-machine named folder groups (planning store + code repos) opened together; never committed.
- **Not built — D11**: designed right after P4 using route evidence. Driving use case is exactly OpenSpec's: the knowledge repo + the code repo open together for implementation sessions. View-equivalents have graded API support (github createProjectV2View ✓, linear/clickup likely, notion/trello ✗).

## What specd adds that NEITHER source has
- **Code-enforced gates** (both sources gate via prompt conventions) — the store refuses illegal transitions regardless of agent compliance.
- Event-sourced projections with doctor/replay — integrity is checkable, not assumed.
- Sink tier model with 6 adapters + migration from grill knowledge stores.
- Execution seam: worktree isolation, [P]-wave scheduling, reviewer subagents, review-gated completion — the complex-features mitigations as native architecture.
- Conventional naming across branches/issues/PRs/commits; `/spec export` handoff; readiness matrix onboarding.

## Honest gaps (v1)
1. Creative exploration (parallel implementations) — deferred (design non-goal).
2. Customization surfaces (presets/extensions/bundles) — deferred (design non-goal).
3. Stores registry + references + worksets — deferred to D11 (the one structural gap vs OpenSpec).
4. Assess-style label-triggered intake workflow — deferred (interactive explore covers it).
5. Convergence vs constitution: converge appends tasks but does not programmatically evaluate constitution principles (parity with spec-kit — both human-governed).

**Overall verdict: the original idea is implemented — every adopted concept is built and the flagship differentiator (event-sourced persistence subsuming all three spec-kit persistence models) is verified live. # Layer taxonomy + stage re-entries — the speckit vocabulary, specd-shaped

**Context.** The post-route review (val-0002) mapped specd against its original idea sources (spec-kit concepts/guides, OpenSpec stores/worksets). The owner named the speckit stage commands as the features wanted most — /constitution, /specify, /plan, /tasks, /implement, /clarify, /analyze — and added a knowledge-layer concept: **product design / business & domain / application** layers, optional per project ("not all projects need all of that, but it is a good exercise").

**Decision 1 — Layer-kind taxonomy.** ITEM_KINDS gains `product`, `domain`, `application` as first-class kinds. `knowledge` is RETIRED as a kind: legacy stores remain readable (rows with the old kind still project fine), but new captures use layers. `constitution` stays its own kind — it IS the product layer's anchor.

- product ← SDLC · user stories · compliance · marketing · purpose
- domain ← use cases · features · flows
- application ← backend · frontend · infra · architecture · technical

**Rejected alternatives:** optional payload tags on knowledge items (queryable but second-class — the owner chose "first-class knowledge categorization"); keeping knowledge alongside the new kinds (two ways to store the same thing; the catch-all survives as a magnet); minimal single-kind addition (half-expresses the three-layer vision).

**Decision 2 — kind.reclassified re-classification.** The heuristic importer (Decision 3) will mis-guess some atoms. A new event type `kind.reclassified` (payload `{kind}`) changes an item's kind via the projection — event-sourced like everything else, doctor-replayable, history preserved, works identically for imported and native items. The target kind must be in ITEM_KINDS (retired `knowledge` refused for NEW captures; re-classification targets the new kinds). **Rejected alternatives:** supersede-flow (duplicates content, breaks link continuity); importer-only (breaks the re-taggable promise).

**Decision 3 — Importer heuristic mapping.** The grill importer maps atom types to layer kinds: dec/ADR → application, req/con → domain, content → product. Wrong guesses are re-classifiable via kind.reclassified. Heuristic accuracy tuning rides real imports. **Blind spots accepted** (owner review): no keyword hints (fragile); the simple type mapping stays.

**Decision 4 — Stage re-entries under /spec.** The speckit stage vocabulary lands as `/spec` subcommands on existing items — NOT as top-level pi commands (that would reverse the one-canonical-command doctrine and crowd the namespace):
- `/spec constitution` — create/review/update the constitution standalone
- `/spec clarify <spec-id>` — targeted clarification loop on an existing spec (evidence/decisions appended)
- `/spec plan <spec-id>` — plan an approved spec (the "plan" namespace was freed by the /spec sink rename)
- `/spec tasks <spec-id>` — break an approved+planned spec into tasks

The start flow stays the happy path; these are re-entry doors. All are prompt-driven (house pattern) and gate-enforced — the store state machine already allows any-stage work; the entries add discoverability, not capability.

**Rejected alternatives for the form:** top-level stage commands (reverses the doctrine; pi's command namespace is shared with other extensions); capability-confirmation-only (zero code, weakest discoverability); hybrid clarify+constitution only (leaves plan/tasks re-entry undiscoverable).

**Settled seams (owner review, 2026-10-26).**
1. **Boundary rule confirmed**: layer kinds organize KNOWLEDGE only — the pipeline (spec/plan/task/run) is application-layer execution. Product-layer work (docs, marketing artifacts) is NOT tracked as tasks; layers feed the pipeline, they do not flow through it.
2. **Importer blind spots accepted**: the simple dec/ADR → application mapping stays (no keyword hints — fragile); mis-guesses are re-classified via kind.reclassified after import.
3. **Anchors: deferred** — whether product-layer items link part-of → constitution depends on real usage; links stay semantic for now (no taxonomy bookkeeping). Revisit when the product layer has enough items to need structure.

**Consequences.** Schema: ITEM_KINDS + EVENT_TYPES grow (additive; no migration — kind/event strings). Ripples: dashboard grouping, specd_query (layer filter), contract-test vocabulary, importer map, start-flow capture prompts (ask the layer). Sequencing: taxonomy + event first, then the stage re-entries (their prompts reference the layer taxonomy). Named honestly: "plan" stays reserved for the pipeline artifact — the stage re-entry is `/spec plan <spec-id>` (verb + item id disambiguates).","pathScope":"specd","phase":null,"parallel":false,"status":"draft"}
