{"kind":"epic","title":"Specd workflow overhaul","body":"## Intent
Make specd feel like an owned, human-driven SDLC tool instead of a one-shot generator: never dirty the developer's git tree, keep project history connected (PR↔issue), support agile shaping (user stories, mermaid diagrams), orchestrate agents as one coordinated run, respect token budgets, support learning-by-doing, and make every state advance the human's verified decision.

## User stories
- As a developer using specd on main, I want store state out of my working tree, so pulls and merges never block on specd artifacts.
- As a developer reviewing history, I want every PR to reference the issue it closes, so the project story is traceable from GitHub.
- As a planner, I want specs to carry user stories and mermaid diagrams, so design reads like an SDLC document.
- As a token-conscious user, I want lean/balanced/full agent depth, so orchestration cost scales with my budget.
- As a learner, I want a Q&A mode that explains the project without writing code, so I can learn by doing the work myself.
- As an owner, I want every gate advance to require my verified sign-off (with an autonomy mode for agentic runs), so the product feels mine.

## Requirements (epic-level, testable)
1. Running any specd command never leaves the git working tree dirty.
2. Worktree sessions resolve the same store as the main checkout.
3. Existing stores (dotpi, lingua-lair, stoa) have a documented, tested migration path.
4. PRs opened by specd reference their task's exported issue via `Closes #N` in the body.
5. Spec template supports User stories and Mermaid diagrams sections.
6. Task runs are coordinated by a single coordinator agent with structured worker briefs/results.
7. Agent depth presets (lean/balanced/full) exist and are config-selectable.
8. Gate advances support machine-verified human sign-off with an explicit autonomy mode for agentic runs.
9. A Q&A learn mode answers project questions without writing code or mutating state.

## Acceptance criteria
- All seven slice specs approved; slices shipped in roadmap order.
- On a migrated existing store, git status stays clean through a full spec→run cycle.

## Out of scope
- Generated learning briefs in issues (rejected: pollutes shared issues with other collaborators).
- External git-repo store as the only option (remains a supported alternative).","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"roadmap","title":"Specd overhaul roadmap","body":"## Ordered slices (flaw → slice, 1:1)
1. **S1 — Store placement & migration** (flaw 1): worktree-aware store resolution; external store registration; migration path for existing in-repo stores (dotpi, lingua-lair, stoa); zero-dirty-tree guarantee.
2. **S2 — PR↔issue linkage** (flaw 2): `Closes #N` in PR body at open_pr; issue recorded in pr.created payload.
3. **S3 — SDLC spec template** (flaw 3): User stories + Mermaid diagrams sections in the spec template; flow docs updated.
4. **S4 — Coordinator orchestration** (flaw 4): single coordinator agent owns a task run; sequential workers with tight briefs; coordinator records store events. Depends on S1.
5. **S5 — Agent depth presets** (flaw 5): lean/balanced/full presets scaling worker context, review scope, output verbosity. Depends on S4.
6. **S6 — Verified gate sign-off** (flaw 7): machine-verified human confirmation for gate advances with artifact preview; per-repo/run autonomy mode. Depends on S1.
7. **S7 — Learn Q&A mode** (flaw 6): read-only Q&A command grounded in store + repo; zero mutations. Independent.

## Rationale
S1 first — every other slice builds on stable, non-polluting store placement. S2/S3/S7 are small independent wins. S4 rebuilds the run pipeline; S5 tunes its cost; S6 adds the human-verification layer once the pipeline shape is settled.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S1: Store placement & migration","body":"## Intent
Running specd must never leave the git working tree dirty, and every session — main checkout or specd-created worktree — must see the same store. Today `events.jsonl` is deliberately tracked in-repo (store.ts writes `*` + `!.gitignore` + `!events.jsonl`), which blocks pulls/merges with uncommitted specd state, and worktree sessions fall back to a fresh `{worktree}/.spec` because store resolution has no worktree mapping.

## User stories
- As a developer on main, I want pulls and merges to never fail on specd artifacts, so my git flow is untouched.
- As a developer inside a task worktree, I want to see the same store as main, so state is never forked.
- As a maintainer of dotpi, lingua-lair, and stoa, I want a migration path for existing stores, so history survives the change.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. Store resolution maps any git worktree to its main repository (via the git common dir) before registry lookup, so registry entries for the main path apply inside worktrees. Test: open the store from a worktree → same store directory as the main checkout.
2. Registered external stores leave zero files in the repository working tree. Test: run a full cycle (create→spec→task→event) against an external store, then `git status --porcelain` is empty.
3. In-repo stores stop tracking store files: the generated `.gitignore` ignores everything under the store dir including `events.jsonl`; store files are machine-local. Test: any specd command against an in-repo store leaves the tree clean.
4. A migration path moves an existing in-repo store to a registered external store by replaying `events.jsonl` into the new location. Test: migrate a fixture store → item, event, and link counts identical; projected statuses identical.
5. The store setup flow (status/register interview) recommends the external store as the default for new repos; in-repo remains a supported option.
6. Migrating a repo removes `.spec/` from the tree and drops the `!.spec/` gitignore re-inclusion where present. Test: after migration, no `.spec/` path appears in `git status` or the tracked file list.

## Mermaid diagrams
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[specd command, cwd] --> B{cwd in a worktree?}
  B -- yes --> C[resolve git common dir → main repo path]
  B -- no --> D[main repo path]
  C --> E[registry lookup]
  D --> E
  E -- registered --> F[external store dir]
  E -- unregistered --> G["{main repo}/.spec"]
  F --> H[open store]
  G --> H
```

## Acceptance criteria
- Worktree and main checkout share one store (no fresh store created inside a worktree).
- Migration replay reproduces identical logical state (items, events, links, statuses).
- No specd operation dirties the working tree in any store mode.
- dotpi, lingua-lair, and stoa each migrate with history intact.

## Out of scope
- Cross-machine sync of external stores via remote push/pull (external-git already exists; not redesigned here).
- Changing the event-sourced storage format itself.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S2: PR↔issue linkage","body":"## Intent
PRs opened by specd must reference the issue they close, so GitHub keeps the project history connected from the PR side. Today `pr.created` records no issue reference in the PR body.

## User stories
- As a developer reviewing PR activity, I want each PR to show the issue it closes, so I can trace task → issue → PR → merge in one place.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. When the task has an exported GitHub issue, `specd_open_pr` includes `Closes #<n>` in the PR body. Test: open a PR for a task with an exported issue → body contains `Closes #n`.
2. When the task has no exported issue, `specd_open_pr` proceeds without a `Closes` line (no error, no placeholder). Test: PR body for an unexported task has no `Closes` line.
3. The `pr.created` event payload records the linked issue number when present. Test: event payload includes the issue number for exported tasks.

## Acceptance criteria
- A specd PR merged on GitHub shows its linked issue as closed, and the issue's timeline references the PR.

## Out of scope
- Branch naming changes (explicitly rejected in interview: body only).
- Commit trailers / `Refs:` footers.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S3: SDLC spec template (stories + mermaid)","body":"## Intent
Specs should read like SDLC documents: user stories and mermaid diagrams alongside intent and requirements, so developers absorb design visually and slice work the agile way instead of receiving a one-shot checklist dump.

## User stories
- As a planner, I want each spec to open with the stories it serves, so the why is never lost.
- As a developer picking up a slice, I want a mermaid flow/architecture diagram in the spec, so I understand the shape before reading code.
- As a specd maintainer, I want the interview template updated once, so every future spec captures stories and diagrams by default.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. The spec template gains a **User stories** section (`As a…, I want…, so that…`). Test: template text contains the section with format guidance.
2. The spec template gains a **Mermaid diagrams** section with guidance (flow/architecture where meaningful; optional for trivial slices). Test: template contains the section.
3. Mermaid blocks pass through specd's read/render paths (report, promote to md, consistency) unmodified. Test: a spec containing a fenced mermaid block reports and promotes without mangling the fence.
4. The fast-path/interview flow docs are updated to ask for stories and diagrams when filling the template.
5. Existing specs without the new sections remain valid. Test: an old-format spec opens, reports, and passes consistency with no errors.

## Acceptance criteria
- A spec created through the flow contains User stories and Mermaid diagrams sections; existing specs still open cleanly.

## Out of scope
- First-class story/diagram item kinds (rejected: too much ceremony).
- Rendering mermaid to images.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S4: Coordinator orchestration","body":"## Intent
A task run should be one coordinated effort, not agents working separately. A single coordinator agent owns the run: it dispatches workers sequentially with tight, self-contained briefs, carries decisions and results forward in its own context, and records store events itself — no state lost between handoffs.

## User stories
- As a developer running a task, I want one agent accountable end-to-end (work → review → PR), so I brief one party and trace one transcript.
- As the coordinator, I hold all prior phase results in context, so the reviewer already knows what the worker did and why.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. `/spec run` assigns the run to a single coordinator agent that executes phases in order (implement → review → PR) within one session context. Test: a run appends `work.started`, `review.completed`, `pr.created` in order, all from one coordinator transcript.
2. Workers receive self-contained briefs — task body, `path_scope`, acceptance criteria, and only task-relevant context — and return structured results the coordinator consumes. Test: brief contains task body + scope + AC; worker result arrives as a parseable structured summary.
3. The coordinator records store events directly after each phase (no second agent re-reading store state to catch up). Test: store events appear with no intermediate read-only reconciliation pass.
4. A worker failure stops the run and hands back to the human with a clear pause summary; the coordinator does not spawn improvised recovery agents. Test: injected worker failure → run paused with a human-readable handback.

## Mermaid diagrams
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Human
  participant C as Coordinator
  participant W as Worker
  participant S as Store
  H->>C: /spec run task-XXXX
  C->>S: work.started
  C->>W: brief (body, scope, AC)
  W-->>C: structured result
  C->>W: review brief (diff-scoped)
  W-->>C: review result
  C->>S: review.completed
  C->>S: pr.created (Closes #N)
  C-->>H: run summary
```

## Acceptance criteria
- One run = one coordinator, ordered phases, store current after each phase, single transcript.

## Out of scope
- Intra-task parallel worker waves (`specd_schedule` already covers cross-task parallelism).
- Multi-agent debate/council review.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S5: Agent depth presets (lean/balanced/full)","body":"## Intent
Agent cost must scale with the user's budget. Depth presets — lean, balanced, full — control how much context workers receive, how much reviewers re-read, and how verbose outputs are. Today's behavior is the `full` ceiling; token-constrained users need the lean floor.

## User stories
- As a token-conscious user, I want a lean preset that reviews only the diff and trims briefs, so a full run fits a small budget.
- As a user with room to spend, I keep full for maximum thoroughness.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. Depth presets `lean|balanced|full` are configurable per repo, with `balanced` applied when unset. Test: preset read from config; default applied when absent.
2. **Lean**: worker briefs carry only task body + `path_scope` (no extra context); review re-reads only changed files; outputs capped to findings (no restatement). Test: lean brief excludes extra context; reviewer scope limited to the diff; output below a documented cap.
3. **Balanced**: briefs include task body, scope, AC, and a bounded context digest; review re-reads changed files plus direct touched-context. Test: balanced brief includes AC and a digest but not full files.
4. **Full**: current behavior preserved. Test: full brief matches today's brief shape.
5. The active preset is stated in the run summary/brief so runs are auditable. Test: run output names the preset.

## Acceptance criteria
- Switching presets measurably changes brief size and review scope; default is `balanced`; `full` is behavior-preserving.

## Out of scope
- Token metering/telemetry dashboards.
- Per-phase preset overrides.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S6: Verified gate sign-off","body":"## Intent
State advances should be the human's verified decision, not the agent's record-keeping. Gate-advancing events gain machine-verified human confirmation with an artifact preview — while an explicit autonomy mode keeps agentic runs friction-free. This is the ownership fix: AI drafts, the human owns every transition.

## User stories
- As an owner, I approve each artifact while seeing exactly what I'm approving (spec body, plan, export target, PR title/body), so the product feels mine.
- As an agentic user, I flip autonomy mode so long runs advance without per-gate interruption.
- As an auditor, I want verified events to record that a human confirmed them, so provenance is trustworthy.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. Gate-advancing events (`explore.decided`, `spec.approved`, `task.exported`, `review.completed`) can require machine-verified human confirmation rendered by the extension, previewing the artifact being approved. Test: in verified mode, an agent appending the event without confirmation is refused with a reason naming the required sign-off.
2. Enforcement is mode-selectable per repo/run: `verified` (default for interactive use) and `autonomous` (agent may self-record; today's behavior). Test: autonomous mode appends without confirmation; verified mode refuses unconfirmed appends.
3. Informational events (`evidence.added`, `decision.made`, `question.answered`, `body.updated`, `work.*`) remain agent-writable in all modes. Test: verified mode still appends `evidence.added` without confirmation.
4. Verified events record their provenance (e.g. payload `source: "human-signoff"`). Test: confirmed events carry the marker; autonomous events carry `source: "agent"`.
5. The mode in effect is visible in the run/session summary. Test: summary names the active mode.

## Acceptance criteria
- In verified mode, every state advance traces to a human confirmation with an artifact preview; autonomous mode is indistinguishable from today's behavior.

## Out of scope
- Remote/async approvals (email, web hooks).
- Fine-grained per-event-type toggles beyond the two modes.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"spec","title":"S7: Learn Q&A mode","body":"## Intent
A mode for learning by doing: ask questions about the project, specs, and technical unknowns, and get grounded answers — while no agent writes code or mutates anything. For users who want to understand their own project (and the tech it uses) instead of delegating.

## User stories
- As a learner, I ask "how does the store replay work?" and get an answer grounded in the actual spec/code, then go do the work myself.
- As a cautious user, I want hard proof the learn session changed nothing.

## Requirements (numbered, testable)
1. A specd learn command opens a Q&A session scoped to the repo: answers draw from the store (specs, plans, tasks, decisions) and repo context. Test: a question about an existing spec is answered with accurate references to it.
2. The session is strictly read-only: it cannot create or modify items, events, or files. Test: store event count and `git status` are unchanged after a learn session.
3. Questions may target a specific item id (e.g. a task or spec) for focused context. Test: targeting `task-0001` grounds the answer in that task's body and history.
4. The learn mode is discoverable from the store/flow docs alongside the other modes.

## Acceptance criteria
- A user runs a full learn session (5+ questions, including one targeted at an item) with zero mutations to store or repo.

## Out of scope
- Auto-generated learning briefs (rejected in interview: they'd leak into shared issues).
- Interactive tutorials/quizzes.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"plan","title":"S1 plan: store placement & migration","body":"## Technical approach
1. **Worktree-aware resolution** (`registry.ts`): `resolveStoreDir(cwd)` maps a linked git worktree to its main repository (via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`) *before* registry lookup and before the `{repo}/.spec` default — so registry entries and in-repo stores resolve identically from any worktree. Pure function; fixture-repo tests follow the existing `test/worktree-*.test.ts` patterns.
2. **Machine-local in-repo stores** (`store.ts:143`): the generated `.gitignore` stops re-including `events.jsonl` (becomes `*` + `!.gitignore`) — zero tracked files, zero dirty tree, ever.
3. **Migration path**: register/migrate flow that (a) creates the external store dir + `.specd-store.yaml` marker via existing `createExternalStore`, (b) replays the old `.spec/events.jsonl` into it — the event-sourced replay already rebuilds full state, no `store.db` copy — (c) flips the registry entry to `{type:"external", storePath}`, (d) removes `.spec/` from the tree and strips the `!.spec/` re-inclusion from `.gitignore`. Idempotent; migration verified by item/event/link count equality before the old dir is deleted.
4. **Setup-flow default**: the store status/register interview recommends external for new repos; in-repo stays supported.
5. **Docs**: store placement guide — external default, in-repo supported, migration steps for dotpi/lingua-lair/stoa.

## Key decisions
- Worktree mapping resolves the git common dir before registry lookup.
- Migration replays `events.jsonl`; never copies `store.db`.
- In-repo stores become fully machine-local (no tracked store files).
- External is the recommended default for new repos.

## Constitution anchor
Serves constitution-0001 (reproducible config as code, guardrails): the guardrail is a git tree that specd never dirties.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"plan","title":"S2 plan: PR↔issue linkage","body":"## Technical approach
1. `openPr` (`sinks/github/pr.ts`) reads the task's history for `task.exported` and extracts `externalRef` — the GitHub issue number is already in the payload (`exec-tools.ts:119` records it at export time).
2. When an `externalRef` exists, the composed PR body gains a trailing `Closes #<externalRef>`; when absent, the body is unchanged (no error, no placeholder).
3. The `pr.created` event payload records the linked issue number when present, so the store history carries the linkage too.
4. Tests: fixture store with an exported task → body contains `Closes #n` and payload carries the number; fixture without export → body unchanged.

## Key decisions
- Linkage lives in PR body composition only — branch naming and commit trailers were explicitly rejected in interview.

## Constitution anchor
Serves constitution-0001: project history stays traceable from the GitHub side, matching the "mirrored, reviewable" ethos.","pathScope":null,"phase":null,"parallel":false}

{"kind":"task","title":"watchChecks misclassifies no-CI repos as failed (gh writes "no checks reported" to stderr)","body":"## Problem
`watchChecks` (packages/specd/src/sinks/github/pr.ts:~184-230) runs `gh pr checks <branch> --json name,bucket`. When the repo has no CI, gh prints "no checks reported on the '…' branch" **to stderr** with exit 1. The implementation only tests `e.stdout` against NO_CHECKS_REPORTED, so the match never happens and exit 1 falls through to `CHECK_EXIT[1] = "failed"`. specd_watch_checks then reports "CI checks failed" for repos with zero configured checks — the exact case the tool description says must map to `pending`.

Verified on PR #28 (dotpi): `gh pr checks … --json name,bucket` → stdout empty, stderr "no checks reported…", exit 1; combined commit status pending with 0 statuses and 0 check-runs; PR MERGEABLE.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `watchChecks` returns `{state: "pending", failing: []}` when gh exits 1 with "no checks reported" — regardless of whether the message arrives on stdout or stderr.
2. Real failing checks (bucket=fail rows) still map to state "failed" with names listed.
3. Passing checks still map to "passed".
4. Regression test: a fake gh runner emitting the message on stderr with exit 1 → pending; emitting fail rows → failed with names.

## Out of scope
Redesigning the CHECK_EXIT mapping beyond this fix.","pathScope":"packages/specd/src/sinks/github/pr.ts, packages/specd/test/","phase":null,"parallel":false,"foundDuring":"task-0020 CI watch on PR #28","type":"fix"}

{"kind":"task","title":"External store registration gaps: register action never creates the store; ~ not expanded; stale committed option in status prompt","body":"## Problem
Three gaps in the external-store registration path, surfaced by the task-0021 docs review (all verified against merged code from #28):

1. `ensureExternalStore` (src/store/external.ts) is exported but never called. `specd_store(action="register", type="external", storePath=…)` (src/tools/sink-tools.ts) only writes the registry entry; the store dir is created lazily by openStore, which writes the in-repo-style `.gitignore` (`*` + `!.gitignore`) and never creates the `.specd-store.yaml` marker or runs `git init`. So a freshly-registered external store does not match the documented file map (marker + events.jsonl tracked in the store's own git) — only migrated stores do.
2. `storePath` is not `~`-expanded in `registerStore`/`migrateToExternalStore` (registry.ts has `expandHome`, used only by reference helpers). `storePath="~/…"` creates a literal `~` directory.
3. `specd_store` status prompt (sink-tools.ts:~124) still lists "In this repo (.spec/, committed)" as an option — stale after in-repo stores became machine-local; contradicts the status output's own recommendation text.

## Acceptance criteria
1. `register` with type=external/external-git runs `ensureExternalStore(storePath, repo)` so the registered store dir exists with marker + git repo + events.jsonl-tracking .gitignore before the registry entry is written.
2. `register` and `migrate` expand `~` in storePath (reuse expandHome).
3. Status prompt no longer offers a committed in-repo option; in-repo documented as machine-local.
4. Fixture tests: register-external creates marker+git store; `~/` storePath resolves under $HOME; status prompt text asserts.

## Out of scope
Migration flow changes beyond the expandHome call.","pathScope":"packages/specd/src/store/external.ts, packages/specd/src/store/registry.ts, packages/specd/src/tools/sink-tools.ts, packages/specd/test/","phase":null,"parallel":false,"foundDuring":"task-0021 review round 1 (specd-reviewer)","type":"fix"}
